reason: The changed journey is Workbench Notes entry through selection, editing, save feedback, link search, and reload. Core owns saved observations; WorkspaceContext owns project/resource readiness; NotesPanel owns the transient draft and picker state. The shared WorkspaceContext change is reviewed through 12 collected recovery cases, including notes publication while Evidence is held, and a real-Core LAN browser case. The 16 collected NotesPanel cases cover loading, no duplicate fetch, bounded link search, autosave, failure/retry, refresh, and selection. Eight collected Notes layout cases cover desktop/compact and emulated Chromium/WebKit at 320/390/430 px. One existing real-Core LAN case covers save/reload, and three permanent real-Core browser projects cover independent readiness and a synthetic 29,000-item Evidence list. The disposable production-bundle benchmark records four switches before and after repair.
exclusions: No Python or Rust behavior changes, so those layers are omitted. The new real-Core test uses live Core for notes and a held synthetic Evidence response to isolate browser loading; no live provider or external target is called. Unrelated workspace and browser journeys and full suites are excluded after reviewing the shared context impact. Physical devices are unavailable; mobile runs use permanent emulated profiles.
